transcript.text: Good to have everyone here. Before we give our readout to the Legal Director, I need to flag an important IP issue I uncovered overnight. The university supplied their controlling patent schedule late last night, and I've identified three background patents — U1, U2, and U3 — that are currently licensed to us only for noncommercial academic use under their master research agreement. As the draft stands, it would grant the university an exclusive commercial license to all background technology, which would inadvertently sweep these three patents into a commercial license that we don't actually have commercial rights to. I have not yet had a chance to incorporate this finding into the draft or circulate it, so I want to make sure we address this before any approval moves forward.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a clinical-data privacy issue before we give our readout. In a working session yesterday with the product lead and privacy office, we confirmed that the company's non-negotiable position is: publication containing patient-level data must be prohibited, and de-identification is required before any permitted external publication. The working-session minutes haven't been circulated to the deal team yet, so this hasn't been reflected in the current draft.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you both for flagging these issues. Both are critical and need to be resolved before I can approve this agreement. Elias, the background IP issue is a serious one — we cannot grant the university an exclusive commercial license to patents U1, U2, and U3 when we only hold noncommercial academic rights to them under the master research agreement. That would create a representation we can't stand behind. The draft needs to carve out those three patents from the exclusive commercial license grant, or we need to negotiate separate commercial rights with the university before signing. Nadia, the publication restriction is equally important — patient-level data must be prohibited in any publication, and de-identification must be required as a precondition to any permitted external publication. That needs to be reflected in the agreement text. Here's what I need before I'll sign off: First, Elias, please revise the background IP section to exclude U1, U2, and U3 from the exclusive commercial license and circulate the updated draft to the deal team. Second, Nadia, please circulate the working-session minutes to the deal team and incorporate the publication and de-identification requirements into the draft. Once both of those revisions are in the draft and reviewed, I can give final approval. I will not approve the agreement as it currently stands.
transcript.speaker: A1
